messages.subject: Double x grid in ggplot2
parts:
Dear ggplot2 folks,
I Never got an answer from R-Help for this.
Why does this plot have extra vertical grid lines at -1, 9,19,29,39,49? How do I get rid of them? I am fearful that the boxplots and the jittered points are being plotted at different locations. How does one debug this?
When I run Dennis's example, I still get the double grid, which does not work as I expect.
Thanks,
Jim Rome

-----------------------------------

On 6/10/2011 7:06 PM, Dennis Murphy wrote:

This toy example works as you seem to expect:

library(ggplot2) 
dat <- data.frame(time = factor(rep(0:59, each = 100), levels = 0:59),

                   error = rnorm(6000))
qplot(time, error, data = dat, size = I(1), main =" title",
      ylab="Error (min)", xlab="Time before ON (min)", alpha=I(1/10),
      geom="jitter") +
geom_boxplot(alpha=.5, color="blue", outlier.colour="green",
             outlier.size=1) +

scale_x_discrete(breaks = seq(from=0, to=60, by=10))

>

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Double x grid in ggplot2
parts:
After thinking about it some more, I think there is a bug in the
scale_x_discrete documentation. There is says that breaks should be a
numeric vector giving break positions. As we've seen in this thread,
that doesn't work all that well. However, giving breaks as a charactor
vector works better:

qplot(time, error, data = dat, size = I(1), main =" title",
ylab="Error (min)", xlab="Time before ON (min)", alpha=I(1/10),
geom="jitter") +
geom_boxplot(alpha=.5, color="blue", outlier.colour="green",
outlier.size=1) +

scale_x_discrete(breaks = as.character(seq(from=0, to=60, by=10)))

So again, it seems that documentation may not be correct.

All that aside, I think there is some question about whether setting
breaks for categorical variables really makes sense. Putting a break
only every n points (where n is > 1) implies that you can interpolate
the values between breaks. If you can interpolate the values between
breaks, then you basically have a numeric (or at least ordered
factor), and putting that on a discrete scale may not be the best
option. The practical implication of all this is that

dat <- transform(dat, time = as.numeric(as.character(time)))
qplot(time, error, group = time, data = dat, size = I(1), main =" title",

ylab="Error (min)", xlab="Time before ON (min)", alpha=I(1/10),
geom="jitter") +
geom_boxplot(alpha=.5, color="blue", outlier.colour="green",
outlier.size=1) +

scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(from=0, to=60, by=10))

Works just fine.

HTH,
Ista
